correctness.rationale: Direct cube-root filter gives exact three entries of every Gram matrix; the 6-periodic table is checked algebraically; rank-one and coordinate-contrast decompositions give all eigenvalues and multiplicities. For n>=5 each eigenvalue is positive. Two explicit parity-dependent cross-products and a monotone integer inequality prove the strict optimality comparison, with exact Taylor expansion for the asymptotic. The standalone enumerator independently reconstructs 18 full matrices and exact-moment checks 408 cases; this supports, not replaces, the proof. n=4 is excluded because an exceptional eigenvalue vanishes.

evidence: The published single-shell first-band theorem concerns one fixed-weight level, while the Boolean-ball theorem concerns an initial interval of weights; neither is a formula for a complete periodic union. The general theorems of Rao on slice restriction do not assert sharp singular values of these unions.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A periodic residue mask is a sum of noncommuting restricted spectral blocks of many individual shells. The spectral levels of the summands cannot simply be added; the specific cancellation of cross correlations under a cube-root filter produces the two-level collapse. Broad association-scheme harmonic expansions may implicitly subsume the calculation, recorded as a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: Whole periodic Hamming-weight classes are natural deterministic one-third-density masks for low-degree Boolean Fourier recovery, unlike arbitrarily chosen finite patterns. The claim classifies all three permitted masks in every dimension n>=5, proves a non-obvious 2-versus-3 spectral sector collapse, and identifies the only condition-optimal design choices and exact exponentially small conditioning loss. It is an exact natural-parameter sampling design theorem, not a mere finite instance, renaming, or a bounded numerical improvement.
